summary.oneLiner: Global provider of enterprise AI, digital, and cloud services helping organisations across healthcare, retail, manufacturing, higher education, financial services, and the public sector derive measurable, sustainable value from their technology investments.
summary.business: Mastek is a global IT services company delivering digital experience, digital engineering, cloud implementation, data, automation, artificial intelligence, and managed services, with a presence in over 40 countries including the UK, US, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia Pacific. It serves close to 400 active customers, predominantly mid-sized businesses and Fortune 1000 companies, through long-standing technology partnerships with Oracle, Salesforce, Microsoft, AWS, Snowflake, and Databricks, deployed via a workforce of more than 4,500 professionals.

currentContext.strengths: Strong global technology partnerships (Oracle, Salesforce, Microsoft, AWS, Snowflake, Databricks) enabling scalable, innovation-driven delivery|Deep client relationships and depth of vertical and domain understanding aiding growing global presence|Well-experienced leadership and a strong talent pool|Integrated ESG framework embedded across operations and strategy|Healthy deal pipeline and strong order backlog supporting revenue visibility and growth|Recognised leadership positioning by analyst firms (Gartner, ISG, Everest Group, IDC, Avasant) across industry and technology capability categories
currentContext.strategies: Account centricity: consolidating the client portfolio from broad-based diversification to high-intensity engagement with the top 50 strategic accounts, structured into dedicated pods with specialised solutioning and delivery teams to increase wallet share and improve Net Revenue Retention.|Vertical-led differentiation across Healthcare (advancing from back-office support to end-to-end 'bed-office' transformation), Manufacturing (IT/OT convergence via ABB and Siemens partnerships), and BFSI & Public Sector (Middle East, Asia, Australia, Saudi Arabia).|Diversifying the digital core: reducing Oracle-led revenue concentration from ~82-85% today toward a more balanced ~75% Oracle / 25% Non-Oracle mix, driven by Salesforce, Microsoft, and Data & AI capabilities.|Establishing Manila as the strategic 'Hub of Excellence' for the Asian delivery footprint, anchoring the Microsoft service-line strategy and supporting growth in Philippines banking and data technology.|Fresher-first hiring strategy: ramping up recruitment in Tier-3 Indian cities, training technical and commerce graduates to become vertical-specific prompt experts.|AI-first talent evolution: transitioning developers from manual coding (Java/Python) toward prompt engineering and domain-led architecture, and industrialising internal AI ('Service-as-a-Software') via a self-built AI-native HRMS and intelligent recruitment/onboarding agents before rolling solutions out to clients.|Simplifying promotion policies to remove hierarchical bias in favour of transparent, merit-based career pathways.|Diversification of AMEA delivery across ANZ, ASEAN, and Asia hubs, and strengthening offshore delivery resilience (e.g., Manila Hub), to mitigate Middle East geopolitical risk.|The Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy, in line with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations and the Companies Act, aimed at bringing transparency to dividend declarations and protecting investor interests.
currentContext.expansion: Mastek is an asset-light IT services business; expansion is expressed through delivery footprint rather than physical capacity. The company operates 20+ global delivery centres under a hybrid onshore-nearshore-offshore model, and during FY26 designated Manila as a new strategic 'Hub of Excellence' for its Asian delivery footprint, anchoring the Microsoft service-line strategy and supporting the growing Philippines client base (banking and data technology). FY26 capex activity was weighted toward sustainability/green-infrastructure investment, including the Leeds office refurbishment for a green-infrastructure upgrade, energy-efficient IT equipment procurement, deployment of an AI-powered carbon accounting platform across the India, UK, Middle East and US offices, SROI dashboard development, and ISO audits to identify energy-saving opportunities; capex directed to such environmental/social-impact technologies rose to 44.06% of total capex in FY26 from 6.7% in FY25.
currentContext.mdna: AI has become the primary driver of global technology spending, with Data Centre Systems and Infrastructure-as-a-Service the fastest-growing segments, underpinning broader enterprise IT services demand.|Generative AI adoption is shifting from pilot projects to enterprise-wide deployment, sustaining investment in AI infrastructure, cloud platforms and intelligent software — a core enabling role for the IT services industry.|UK public sector IT spending is pivoting toward sector-specific precision solutions and agentic AI for productivity despite significant legacy-system constraints, with central government targeting GBP 14 billion in technical efficiency gains by FY29 and GOV.UK One Login expanding digital identity services.|North America IT services market remains innovation-led, driven by enterprise digital transformation, AI adoption, cloud migration and rising cybersecurity investment, with nearshore delivery models helping mitigate talent constraints.|AMEA growth driven by regional recalibration, vertical-led growth (Healthcare, Manufacturing, BFSI & Public Sector) and AI-enabled transformation, alongside diversification away from Oracle-concentrated revenue toward Salesforce, Microsoft and Data & AI.|Profitability grew Y-o-Y supported by AI-led and other cost efficiencies, optimal resource utilisation resulting in higher revenue per FTE, and currency tailwinds, partly offset by a true-up impact in gratuity and leave-encashment benefits following statutory Labour Code changes announced in November 2025.|Management expects revenue growth to outpace headcount growth as continued investment in AI-led delivery efficiencies improves unit cost of delivery.|AMEA business enters FY27 with a robust revenue backlog of 65-70%, providing strong revenue visibility and enabling predictable growth, AI-led delivery efficiencies, and continued verticalisation.

risks.note: Increasing competition across key markets is intensifying pricing pressure, particularly in commoditised service areas, thereby impacting margin expansion potential (flagged as a Threat in MD&A Opportunities and Threats).

Evolving data privacy regulations and cybersecurity exposure are flagged by management as a threat; the Company's Risk Management Framework explicitly covers cyber security and ESG for identification, assessment and monitoring of key risks.

AMEA active clients fell to 398 (consolidated) in FY26 from 466 in FY25 as the Company deliberately reduced smaller, non-strategic accounts and exited selected low-margin engagements; the region did not record revenue growth in FY26 while repositioning toward higher-value, more profitable business.

Operations in parts of the Middle East faced geopolitical uncertainties and timing delays in certain programmes during FY26, though management reports no disruption to client delivery or workforce continuity to date.

risks.risk: Macro / inflationary headwinds in EMEA and Africa
risks.note: Higher energy prices and persistent inflationary pressures affected technology spending in some consumer and hardware segments across the EMEA/Africa markets Mastek serves, per management's regional demand commentary.

risks.risk: Operational complexity of a multi-geography delivery model
risks.note: Mastek Group's presence across multiple geographies, with a large number of employees, suppliers, and delivery partners, requires robust internal controls and scalable processes to manage global-scale operations — cited by the Company as the rationale underpinning its internal financial control and internal audit framework.

one-line thesis: A "predictable" quarter where the order book finally converted into revenue — $104.8 mn (+1.2% QoQ, +1.8% cc), INR 985 cr (+5% QoQ, +7.7% YoY) — with the 12-month backlog at $310 mn, up 13.3% in USD and 25% in INR, and North America's total backlog up 29.8% sequentially on a $25 mn, 5-year Salesforce Agentforce AI deal. The offsets are real and named: Middle East is unravelling on the West Asia crisis (bench cost, delayed collections, a doubtful-debt provision), the NHS England relationship is in a project-transition trough that dragged the top-5 clients down 4% QoQ, and ESOP plus increments will compress margin from Q2. Management will not guide beyond "FY27 should be better than FY26."
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > Adjustments / one-offs: Middle East caused three separate hits inside the EBITDA line — held bench cost as ramp-ups slipped, delayed collections, and unbilled work that could not be invoiced due to client unavailability, leading to a provision for doubtful, described as "a onetime impact in the quarter, which we believe we'll be able to reverse as we go forward down the year." UK regulatory costs and mix change were offset by cost efficiency and a currency tailwind. Separately, an income-tax assessment for FY2022-23 added INR 91 cr (transfer pricing) + INR 32.5 cr (domestic tax) of income — the CFO went out of his way to correct the market: "I'll repeat the word 'income' — that was not a tax demand of INR 135 crore or INR 125 crore… the tax impact will be approximately INR 31 cr." Appeal filed with CIT(A) on 26 June 2026.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: "Our FY27 performance should be better than FY26" — the only forward statement on revenue, immediately hedged with "we generally don't give guidance."
ESOP charge: $400,000–$500,000 per quarter, starting Q2 FY27. Management confirmed it "will rather reduce our EBITDA for the year."

Increments planned in Q2 FY27 — "Q2 margin definitely will be a bit impacted because of that." Full-year margin guidance explicitly withheld, with a commitment that internal cost efficiencies will "mitigate a significant portion of the impact."

North America turns into a growth engine by H2 FY27 — stated three separate times: the $25 mn deal ramps in H2 FY27; "by H2 is where we believe North America should turn itself into a growth engine"; US Healthcare & Life Sciences turnaround "especially as we get into H2, we are quite sure."

UK Healthcare (NHS) returns to sequential growth from Q2 FY27 — "will start ramping back up in the right direction from Q2 and as we get into H2. It should be at the same levels and growing from there."
North America margin: mid-teens once the geography reaches a $28–30 mn per quarter run-rate.
Middle East: "should at least stay flat" as already-won projects ramp; return to growth only if the geopolitical situation stabilises.
FCA deal already ramping, with more ramp-up in Q2; HADES was a renewal (no incremental ramp); the $25 mn NA deal ramps H2 FY27.
Subcon cost stable at ~18.5% of revenue. Discounting on renewals at ~15% typical (20-25% in one or two cases), explicitly not the 50% peers have called out.
AI maturity assessment of the entire installed customer base to be completed in the next 90–180 days.
order book & pipeline: 12-month backlog $310 mn, +3.2% QoQ, +13.3% YoY USD / +25% INR — three consecutive quarters of NA order-book improvement.

$25 mn, 5-year Salesforce Agentforce AI transformation deal in North America — "one of our largest deals in the recent quarters," a TCV event rather than an ACV one. An analyst noted that excluding it, total backlog was flat sequentially; management did not dispute the arithmetic but pointed to healthy TCV direction.
40+ new AI-led opportunities closed in the quarter.
Middle East: a large Healthcare deal closed in Q1 with "a few more large Healthcare deals in our pipe, which we should close very soon" — but ramp timing is uncertain.
Named UK deals: FCA (ramping, driving the BFSI revenue recovery), Atlas, HADES (renewal of an existing customer, steady revenue not incremental).

Management notes a structural change: "we did not have as many number of large deal opportunities in our pipe across geographies" before — large-deal pipeline count is now materially higher and described as well-qualified.
segment / subsidiary detail: UK — the foundation. +3% QoQ cc, EBIT ~20%. BFSI is now converting Q4's order-book strength into revenue. Public sector grew 7.9% sequentially on stable existing customers plus new local-government wins; a political leadership change in the country is being watched for budget/policy implications.

UK Healthcare (NHS England): the swing factor. Old projects closed out while new ones started — "a timing gap" that pulled top-5 clients down 4% QoQ and 12% YoY. The new work is in data modernisation and building the NHS data platform, i.e. higher-value than what it replaced.
North America: +2% QoQ cc, +6% INR. Third consecutive quarter of strong order book; focus vertical is Healthcare & Life Sciences. Still sub-scale for margin — needs $28-30 mn/quarter.

Middle East (AMEA): "severe headwinds" from the West Asia crisis. Order book did get signed late in the quarter but ramp predictability is poor and the environment re-deteriorated "in the last couple of weeks" before the call.
Service lines: Data, Automation & AI grew 9.8% sequentially — the fastest-growing line and the strategic centre of gravity.
growth verticals / optionality: AI-led demand across three motions: (1) existing customers — an internal AI maturity model rating clients Level 0-5, driving roadmaps from AI foundations (governance, security, compliance) through SDLC/testing adoption to enterprise-wide transformation; (2) net-new via Oracle, Salesforce, Snowflake and Databricks partnerships; (3) "AI for tech" — going in as champion-challenger against incumbent large vendors on price competitiveness.
Service-as-a-Software: transforming SaaS into non-SaaS AI-native builds — both a client offering and Mastek's own internal programme.

Mastek as Customer Zero: the company has replaced its own CRM, recruitment and payables systems with AI-native "systems of intelligence," targeting recruitment cycle time, win predictability and G&A cost — and is reusing these as client case studies.

Workforce re-shaping: a large portion of engineering resources and domain consultants are being converted into FDEs (forward deployed engineers) and FDDCs (forward deployed domain consultants), some already embedded in live projects.
6a. moat & competitive position: UK public sector and NHS depth — described as "our core pillar," with vertical insight in healthcare and public sector that "creates a phenomenal position for Mastek to take AI transformation lead in select verticals."
UK EBIT of ~20% demonstrates genuine pricing power in that geography, against a group operating EBITDA of 15.4%.

Discounting discipline as evidence of positioning: while peers report renewal discounts exceeding 50%, Mastek's are "generally 15%… 20%-25% tops in 1 or 2 cases" — it is not being forced into the worst of the price war.

The combination management claims is rare: enterprise application transformation + a strong data practice + engineering — "which makes us uniquely positioned to become a transformation company, starting these transformations from back office and then taking them forward into the entire business."
margins & cost dynamics: 15.4% operating EBITDA was hit by the Middle East trio (bench, collections, doubtful provision) plus UK regulatory costs and mix, partly offset by cost efficiency and currency. The forward pressure is fully disclosed and additive: ESOP $400-500k/quarter from Q2 (an analyst's ~25 bps estimate went unchallenged) plus Q2 increments. Management refused a full-year margin number but committed to internal cost efficiencies as the offset. Two structural margin levers were named: North America crossing $28-30 mn/quarter for mid-teens margins, and fixed-bid/outcome-focused contracts, where "our ability to execute them faster and better is also improving… we should be able to execute them at a much better margin than we see them today." Utilisation excluding trainees fell 2% sequentially on order pushouts and the Middle East. Subcon steady at 18.5%. Attrition improving (17.4% → 16.4%).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Not a capex business. The expansion is people and capability: headcount +167 (UK +125 on new-project ramp-ups), a new COO hired from LTM to drive delivery transformation and an outcome-focused operating model, and a skill-matrix shift toward FDE/FDDC roles. The prior quarter's stated preference for inorganic M&A for domain capabilities rather than heavy organic capex was not revisited on this call — no acquisition was announced or discussed.
capital allocation: Cash generation is the quiet good news: $116 mn collected, positive operating cash of INR 27 cr despite paying INR 107 cr of variable pay, and net cash/investments up ~INR 200 cr over two quarters on "prudent cash management and aggressive collection initiatives." Against that, the ESOP programme is a deliberate deployment of shareholder value into retention — management defended it on the grounds that "creating a long-term impact also requires a good long-term team," and noted analysts and investors had themselves recommended it. The FY2022-23 tax assessment carries an ~INR 31 cr potential impact, under appeal.
risks & watch-items: Middle East is the acute risk — uncertain deal closures, unpredictable ramp, held bench, delayed collections, and an environment that "has again become a little volatile" in the fortnight before the call.
Client concentration in transition: top-5 down 4% QoQ / 12% YoY on the NHS England project changeover. The recovery is promised for Q2 — a clean, checkable commitment.
Margin is guided down in the near term (ESOP + increments) with no full-year floor given.

AI-led competitive displacement cuts both ways — Mastek is challenging incumbents on others' accounts while "consistently trying to protect our turf on existing customers where we are getting challenged by incumbents." The CEO named this as the key headwind alongside the Middle East.
UK political leadership change — budget and policy priority shifts are being monitored; UK is the largest and most profitable geography.
North America remains sub-scale for margin and had "a lot of projects" ramping down alongside new wins.
management quality / tone: Markedly more upbeat than the prior quarter, and an analyst called that out directly — the CEO's answer was honest and deflationary: "the business is trending in the similar direction that we had seen in Q4… it's not drastically changed from where we were in Q4." He credited the 12-month backlog compounding rather than claiming a demand inflection. The CFO's unprompted correction on the tax assessment (income added, not tax demanded) was a genuine service to the market. Costs were disclosed before being asked about in some cases and quantified when asked (ESOP per quarter, subcon %, discount ranges). The CEO also volunteered a caution alongside the positive FY27 statement — "I'm also giving you a little bit of caution in terms of Middle East." The recurring "phenomenal" vocabulary is promotional, but the substance underneath was consistently specific.
non-obvious takeaways: Backlog growth of 25% YoY in INR vs 13.3% in USD — half the headline order-book growth is currency. The cc revenue growth of 1.8% QoQ is the honest operating number, against +5% in INR.
Ex the $25 mn deal, total backlog was flat sequentially. The AI narrative rests substantially on one large TCV win; the "40+ AI opportunities" are individually small land-and-expand engagements.
The NHS trough is a quality upgrade in disguise — the work that ended was replaced by data modernisation and platform-building for NHS, a structurally better position than the projects that closed.

Mastek is being repriced downward on net-new ("the net new business that we win or compete for is definitely coming at a much more price aggressive positioning") but is betting that faster execution on fixed-bid/outcome contracts recovers the margin. That is the single most important unproven assumption in the story.
The internal Service-as-a-Software transformation is being run as a revenue asset, not just a cost programme — the case studies are explicitly part of the go-to-market.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q4 FY26 (prior): FY27 expected better than FY26 (no specific %); margin guided stable at 16.0-16.1% for FY27; order inflow momentum positive especially NA and UK; focus on inorganic M&A for domain capabilities rather than organic capex.

Q1 FY27 (this): Reaffirmed: "FY27 performance should be better than FY26"; NA and UK order-book momentum continued (NA total backlog +29.8% QoQ, third consecutive strong quarter). Deteriorated vs prior guidance: the 16.0-16.1% FY27 margin guide is effectively withdrawn — Q1 came in at 15.4%, and management now declines to give a full-year margin number while pre-announcing ESOP ($400-500k/quarter from Q2) and Q2 increments as further drags. New commitments: NA becomes a growth engine by H2 FY27; UK Healthcare/NHS returns to sequential growth from Q2 FY27; NA margins mid-teens at a $28-30 mn/quarter run-rate; Middle East to at least stay flat. New this quarter: $25 mn 5-year Salesforce Agentforce deal; 40+ AI opportunities closed; new COO Amit Gajwani; FY2022-23 tax assessment with ~INR 31 cr impact under appeal; Service-as-a-Software internal transformation. M&A: no acquisition discussed, despite the prior quarter's stated inorganic preference.

Q2 FY27 → check: (a) did UK Healthcare/NHS actually return to sequential growth as promised, (b) did the FCA deal ramp further, (c) EBITDA margin after ESOP + increments — how much of the impact was really mitigated, (d) Middle East flat or worse, (e) order intake ex the $25 mn deal, (f) top-5 client concentration recovering from −4% QoQ, (g) any progress on the promised H2 NA turnaround and the $28-30 mn/quarter threshold.

Management refused a full-year margin number but committed to internal cost efficiencies as the offset. Two structural margin levers were named: North America crossing $28-30 mn/quarter for mid-teens margins, and fixed-bid/outcome-focused contracts, where "our ability to execute them faster and better is also improving… we should be able to execute them at a much better margin than we see them today." Utilisation excluding trainees fell 2% sequentially on order pushouts and the Middle East. Subcon steady at 18.5%. Attrition improving (17.4% → 16.4%).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Not a capex business. The expansion is people and capability: headcount +167 (UK +125 on new-project ramp-ups), a new COO hired from LTM to drive delivery transformation and an outcome-focused operating model, and a skill-matrix shift toward FDE/FDDC roles. The prior quarter's stated preference for inorganic M&A for domain capabilities rather than heavy organic capex was not revisited on this call — no acquisition was announced or discussed.
capital allocation: Cash generation is the quiet good news: $116 mn collected, positive operating cash of INR 27 cr despite paying INR 107 cr of variable pay, and net cash/investments up ~INR 200 cr over two quarters on "prudent cash management and aggressive collection initiatives." Against that, the ESOP programme is a deliberate deployment of shareholder value into retention — management defended it on the grounds that "creating a long-term impact also requires a good long-term team," and noted analysts and investors had themselves recommended it. The FY2022-23 tax assessment carries an ~INR 31 cr potential impact, under appeal.
risks & watch-items: Middle East is the acute risk — uncertain deal closures, unpredictable ramp, held bench, delayed collections, and an environment that "has again become a little volatile" in the fortnight before the call.
Client concentration in transition: top-5 down 4% QoQ / 12% YoY on the NHS England project changeover. The recovery is promised for Q2 — a clean, checkable commitment.
Margin is guided down in the near term (ESOP + increments) with no full-year floor given.

AI-led competitive displacement cuts both ways — Mastek is challenging incumbents on others' accounts while "consistently trying to protect our turf on existing customers where we are getting challenged by incumbents." The CEO named this as the key headwind alongside the Middle East.
UK political leadership change — budget and policy priority shifts are being monitored; UK is the largest and most profitable geography.
North America remains sub-scale for margin and had "a lot of projects" ramping down alongside new wins.
management quality / tone: Markedly more upbeat than the prior quarter, and an analyst called that out directly — the CEO's answer was honest and deflationary: "the business is trending in the similar direction that we had seen in Q4… it's not drastically changed from where we were in Q4." He credited the 12-month backlog compounding rather than claiming a demand inflection. The CFO's unprompted correction on the tax assessment (income added, not tax demanded) was a genuine service to the market. Costs were disclosed before being asked about in some cases and quantified when asked (ESOP per quarter, subcon %, discount ranges). The CEO also volunteered a caution alongside the positive FY27 statement — "I'm also giving you a little bit of caution in terms of Middle East." The recurring "phenomenal" vocabulary is promotional, but the substance underneath was consistently specific.
non-obvious takeaways: Backlog growth of 25% YoY in INR vs 13.3% in USD — half the headline order-book growth is currency. The cc revenue growth of 1.8% QoQ is the honest operating number, against +5% in INR.
Ex the $25 mn deal, total backlog was flat sequentially. The AI narrative rests substantially on one large TCV win; the "40+ AI opportunities" are individually small land-and-expand engagements.
The NHS trough is a quality upgrade in disguise — the work that ended was replaced by data modernisation and platform-building for NHS, a structurally better position than the projects that closed.

Mastek is being repriced downward on net-new ("the net new business that we win or compete for is definitely coming at a much more price aggressive positioning") but is betting that faster execution on fixed-bid/outcome contracts recovers the margin. That is the single most important unproven assumption in the story.
The internal Service-as-a-Software transformation is being run as a revenue asset, not just a cost programme — the case studies are explicitly part of the go-to-market.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q4 FY26 (prior): FY27 expected better than FY26 (no specific %); margin guided stable at 16.0-16.1% for FY27; order inflow momentum positive especially NA and UK; focus on inorganic M&A for domain capabilities rather than organic capex.

Q1 FY27 (this): Reaffirmed: "FY27 performance should be better than FY26"; NA and UK order-book momentum continued (NA total backlog +29.8% QoQ, third consecutive strong quarter). Deteriorated vs prior guidance: the 16.0-16.1% FY27 margin guide is effectively withdrawn — Q1 came in at 15.4%, and management now declines to give a full-year margin number while pre-announcing ESOP ($400-500k/quarter from Q2) and Q2 increments as further drags. New commitments: NA becomes a growth engine by H2 FY27; UK Healthcare/NHS returns to sequential growth from Q2 FY27; NA margins mid-teens at a $28-30 mn/quarter run-rate; Middle East to at least stay flat. New this quarter: $25 mn 5-year Salesforce Agentforce deal; 40+ AI opportunities closed; new COO Amit Gajwani; FY2022-23 tax assessment with ~INR 31 cr impact under appeal; Service-as-a-Software internal transformation. M&A: no acquisition discussed, despite the prior quarter's stated inorganic preference.

Q2 FY27 → check: (a) did UK Healthcare/NHS actually return to sequential growth as promised, (b) did the FCA deal ramp further, (c) EBITDA margin after ESOP + increments — how much of the impact was really mitigated, (d) Middle East flat or worse, (e) order intake ex the $25 mn deal, (f) top-5 client concentration recovering from −4% QoQ, (g) any progress on the promised H2 NA turnaround and the $28-30 mn/quarter threshold.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.
